q142_verdicts.claim: Twiggs' profile came from his voluntarily provided buccal swab, used as an elimination sample
q142_verdicts.basis: The split is exactly right on both halves. UPGRADEABLE HALF, day2.txt opened directly: Faumuina at 05:12:26–05:12:51 — Twiggs' DNA 'was obtained by law enforcement officers', by buccal swab (counsel's term, adopted, then defined by her in her own words), 'packaged and sent to the lab for testing in comparison' — 'Yes.' Bakker's elimination language is her own, repeatedly: 'I was submitted an elimination sample from Mr. Twiggs' (06:33:52), 'the field submitted him as an elimination' (07:22:03 — note this string appears twice only because Rev repeats the overlap across 'PART 12 OF 14'; it is ONE utterance, not two), 'I used Mr. Twiggs as an elimination' (07:22:03), 'I used him as an elimination sample' (06:39:11). NON-UPGRADEABLE HALF, day3.txt opened directly: Agent Brian Davis at 01:02:29–01:02:51 — 'I don't recall happening there. I believe it happened later… That was obtained from him'; 'I don't recall if it was there later at his residence'; 'But ultimately a buccal swab was obtained from Mr. Twiggs?' — 'Yes, it was.' The word 'voluntarily' attaches only to the PHONE, at 01:03:00: 'They conducted an interview of him and then he provided his phone. He did it voluntarily also, provided it to those agents' — and even there, prosecutor Hunt's question was 'Do you know if his phone was taken from him?' — 'It was.' NULL RE-RUN WITH A CAPABLE PATTERN: I ran 'voluntar\w*' (capable of matching 'voluntarily', 'voluntary', 'voluntarily provided') across day1–day5 via artifact_search.find, which searches BOTH U+FFFE readings; the defect census reports 0 U+FFFE splits and 0 NUL bytes in all five files, so the two readings are identical here — checked and stated. Results: day1 0; day2 6 distinct (all Robinson's surrender to Washington County); day3 1 (the phone, above); day4 2 (argument about Robinson's statements/admissions); day5 1 (ATF lab accreditation). Nothing attaches voluntariness to the swab. I also verified in BOTH DIRECTIONS: 'consent\w*' across all five days returns one hit (day1, counsel consenting to witness presence in the courtroom), and 'search warrant' returns hits whose only warrant-obtained buccal swabs are TYLER ROBINSON's — day3 at 46:24, 'After a search warrant was granted, his clothing was recovered, along with buccal swabs to collect his DNA', in a passage about Robinson's booking, NOT Twiggs. So the record neither supplies nor contradicts voluntariness for Mr. Twiggs' swab. Cross-checked the affidavit of probable cause, the Information, and the 2026-08-11 defence brief: 'buccal' 0, 'voluntar\w*' 0, 'elimination' 0 in all three, with positive controls confirming the files load and the patterns run ('Twigg\w*' 44 hits in the brief, 'roommate' 10 in the affidavit).
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: SPLIT, as proposed and unchanged. 'Buccal swab' and 'used as an elimination sample' → T1 (day2.txt 05:12:26–05:12:51 Faumuina; 06:33:52 / 07:22:03 Bakker; corroborated day3.txt 01:02:51 Davis). 'Voluntarily' → NOT upgradeable; drop the adverb from the swab, or keep it explicitly at T3 attributed to OANN/Fox with the T1 record noted as saying only that the swab 'was obtained' and that Davis could not recall where. The null is a finding with a stated scope: pattern 'voluntar\w*', all five prelim-hearing day files, both U+FFFE readings (0 splits present), plus 'consent\w*' and 'search warrant' as cross-checks; NOT extended to the press-conference transcripts or the docket export.

q142_verdicts.claim: (New T1 material) The elimination framing did not originate with the laboratory — it was an investigative input
q142_verdicts.basis: All three quoted strings verified verbatim in day2.txt, opened directly: 'the field submitted him as an elimination' (07:22:03); 'I talked to them with regards to if I should utilize Mr. Twiggs as an elimination versus comparing him and offering a statistic' (06:35:32); and, on why she expected his DNA, 'But in talking to the investigators, based on their investigation, it was important to assume potentially Mr. Twiggs was present' (06:37:54). I found two further strings the map did not cite that strengthen it: 'In receiving that sample and talking to the investigators, it was decided that Mr. Twiggs should be used as an elimination' (06:33:52) and 'based on speaking with the investigators, they had information to suspect that that towel came from Mr. Robinson's home and I should utilize Mr. Twiggs as an elimination' (06:38:48). BUT the claim as worded overshoots in one direction and under-reports in another. (1) 'Did not originate with the laboratory' is too absolute: the SAMPLE was submitted by the field, and the DECISION was consultative — 'it was decided' — while Bakker simultaneously asserted her own basis, 'I did use my own knowledge and training to determine that I was going to utilize him as an assumed contributor' (07:22:51) and 'I visually looked at the DNA sample… he also had those peaks' (07:21:25). The supported form is that the input and the framing came from the field and the decision was taken in consultation, not that the laboratory had no part in it. (2) DIRECTION CHECK — the row omits the investigators' stated reason, and it is exculpatory-leaning and must travel with the upgrade: 'Mr. Twiggs was a roommate of Mr. Robinson. And it was thought that those items came from potentially Mr. Robinson's home' (06:37:54). That is a household-provenance rationale, not any suggestion of involvement; published without it, 'investigators told the lab to assume Twiggs was present' invites exactly the inference the record does not support. (3) The countervailing fact belongs with it too: Burt put to her that the towel was found 'in a bush out at the university', and she agreed — 'That is correct. It was found outside of a home' (06:38:48) — while maintaining the investigators' information.
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: T1 for the quoted testimony (day2.txt 06:33:52, 06:35:32, 06:37:54, 06:38:48, 07:22:03), but reworded: 'The elimination sample and the framing came from the field, and the decision to use Mr. Twiggs as an elimination rather than compare him and report a statistic was taken by the examiner in consultation with investigators' — NOT 'did not originate with the laboratory'. Three items must travel in the same passage: the investigators' stated reason (roommate; items thought to have come from the shared home), Bakker's asserted independent visual basis (07:21:25, 07:22:51), and her concession that the towel was found outside a home (06:38:48).

q142_verdicts.claim: (New T1 material) The report is categorical about Twiggs and hedged about Robinson

Counter-search logged: r'Twiggs.{0,300}?interview' and its reverse return zero in day1/day2/day5 under BOTH U+FFFE readings (patterns proven capable — Twigg matches 0/64/5 and interview 1/15/2 in those files), so nothing elsewhere in the hearing record contradicts the date, venue, or recording.
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: T1 — sworn testimony of Agent Brian Davis (Utah State Bureau of Investigation). Cite day3.txt 01:01:55 (occurrence, early-morning timing, St. George PD venue) and day4.txt 02:37:18 (audio/video recorded), NOT the day3 01:03:52 summary premise. Two caveats must travel with the upgrade: (a) Davis was not personally present (day4 02:36:59) — his knowledge is from reviewing the recording and speaking with one attending agent, so this is T1 sworn testimony resting on derivative knowledge, not eyewitness testimony; (b) §7.1 line 188 as currently written says only "initial interview; under use immunity" and does not itself assert "recorded" — the "recorded" assertion lives at profile line 22, so the re-marking must be applied to the right sentence.

q142_verdicts.claim: The September 12, 2025 interview was conducted "under use immunity."
q142_verdicts.basis: The split is right in both halves, and the null is real. Opened day3.txt lines 2015–2027: Hunt "Was Mr. Twiggs given use immunity?" / Davis "Yes, he was." / "By what offices?" / "The Utah County Attorney's Office as well as the United States Attorney's Office." Verbatim as quoted, sworn, T1. Framing quote at line 1991 (01:04:13) also verbatim: "Before Mr. Twiggs' interview on April 20th, 2026...". NULL RE-RUN with a capable pattern: I used stem r'immun' (matches immunity / immunities / immunized / immune — the row's narrower r'immunit' would miss "immune"), under BOTH U+FFFE readings via artifact_search.norm(join=True) and norm(join=False). Counts identical under both readings and identical to the map: day1 0, day2 0, day3 6, day4 1, day5 0. I opened all seven hits. All six day3 hits sit inside the April-20 line of questioning (01:04:13 through 01:05:15). The single day4 hit is line 842 (Rev 02:11:56), the questioner on the played recording saying "you've also been given a federal agreement and a state agreement granting you immunity from prosecution for materials that you discuss now" — "now" is the April 20 interview. Nothing places immunity at September 12. NEW CORROBORATION from a file no row cited and the task flags as never opened: the 2026-06-22 contempt/subpoena hearing transcript (2026-06-23-pub_rev-contempt-hearing-transcript.txt) carries 7 'immun' hits under both readings. Judge Graf recites the defendant's position — cross-examination "concerning ... his immunity agreements with the State and federal prosecutors" — and then, in the court's OWN analysis, "The court does not minimize the significance of immunity agreements as potential sources of bias." That is a second primary artifact carrying a two-office grant. It also carries zero hits for "September 12", "Sept. 12", "9/12" and "April 20" under both readings, so it adds no date attachment either way.
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: T1 for the existence of the use-immunity grant and its two granting offices — day3.txt 01:05:09–01:05:15 (sworn), corroborated by Judge Graf's own analysis in the 2026-06-22 bench ruling. For the September 12 attachment the marking should be STRONGER than the map's "unchanged": §7.1 line 188 positively asserts "September 12, 2025 — initial interview; under use immunity" in the ANALYST layer, and no primary artifact in this library attaches immunity to that date. It must be affirmatively flagged as asserted-not-established (or the clause moved onto the April 20 line), not left sitting at T1 via T3 as though merely un-upgraded. Do not use the day4 02:11:56 on-recording immunity sentence to carry it — see row 5: Graf ruled McBride's recorded statements hearsay, admitted only for context and effect.

q142_verdicts.claim: The April 20, 2026 interview took place at the Utah County Attorney's Office.
q142_verdicts.basis: Tier outcome is right; the row's cited source is a questioner's premise and must be repointed. The quoted string IS present, verbatim, in day4.txt line 1726 — but that whole line is Ms. Hunt's QUESTION at Rev 02:38:40 ("And was this same text thread ... shown to him during his second interview in ... Sorry, let me get the date right. April 20th, 2026 at the Utah County Attorney's Office that we just observed part of in state's Exhibit 16?"). Davis's answer at line 1730 (02:38:58) is "Yes, it was shown to him" — it confirms that the text thread was shown, not the location. Standing alone, that row would be a tier upgrade resting on counsel's premise. The claim survives because the witness gives it himself elsewhere: day3.txt line 1963 (Rev 01:03:29), Hunt "Where was that?" / Davis "Happened at the Utah County Attorney's Office." Open question, witness's own answer, sworn. Davis also lists the attendees at line 1971 (01:03:35). Independent T1 corroboration from a filing no row cited: the defence's 2026-08-11 preliminary-hearing brief describes "a recorded interview between the Utah County Attorney's Office and witness Lance Twiggs, St.Ex. 16" — a primary court filing by the adverse party.
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: T1 — but the citation must be repointed to day3.txt 01:03:29 (Davis's own sworn answer to "Where was that?"), with the defence's 2026-08-11 brief as corroboration. Do NOT cite the day4 02:38:40 passage as the basis: it is Ms. Hunt's question, and the answer it draws goes to the exhibit being shown, not the venue.

q142_verdicts.claim: The April 20 interview was conducted by prosecutor Ryan McBride.
q142_verdicts.basis: Both cited quotes exist, but one locator is wrong. The day4 quote is at Rev 42:09 (day4.txt line 366), not "~00:43" — 43:01 is the next turn and belongs to Mr. Novak. Speaker is Judge Tony F Graf Jr, verbatim: "any video showing anything other than Mr. McBride and Lance Twiggs was to be redacted...". The day3 quote is exact at day3.txt line 2383 (02:41:43): "...the statements of Mr. McBride in State's Exhibit 16 is overruled." Three further supports, one of them sworn: day3 line 1971 (01:03:35) Davis lists McBride among those present; day3 line 2067 (01:06:08) Davis, asked who gave the admonition — "By Ryan McBride with the Utah County Attorney's Office"; day4 line 470 (Rev 50:04) Mr. Novak, arguing — "this questioning by Mr. McBride and the answers to these questions by Mr. Twiggs" (counsel's argument, not sworn, but uncontradicted on the record and consistent with the court's own description). Prosecutor status is on the face of the record: day4 line 210, appearances — "Chad Grunander, Ryan McBride, Lauren Hunt, David Sturgill, Chris Ballard for the state." ROUTE NOTE VERIFIED: inside the played exhibit Rev labels the questioner "Speaker 4" (26 turns) and "Speaker 2" (59 turns) — the same person by content, e.g. Speaker 4 administers the oath at 02:11:13 and Speaker 2 resumes the same questioning at 02:16 — and never names him. Identification comes from the court's own description, exactly as the map says. Two further unnamed voices appear ("Speaker 3" 2 turns, "Speaker 6" 6 turns).
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: T1 — Ryan McBride, prosecutor with the Utah County Attorney's Office, as the interview's principal questioner and the person on camera with Mr. Twiggs. Fix the day4 locator to 42:09 (Graf), not ~00:43. Add the scope limit: at least two other unnamed voices speak on the recording (Rev "Speaker 3" and "Speaker 6"), and Davis's sworn attendee list places five other officials in the room, so "conducted by" carries principal questioner, not sole speaker. Prefer citing Davis's sworn day3 01:06:08 alongside Graf, so the upgrade does not rest solely on judicial and counsel description.

q142_verdicts.claim: "The court later ruled McBride's own statements in the recording were hearsay and directed focus onto Twiggs' answers."
q142_verdicts.basis: Opened day3.txt line 2383, Rev timestamp 02:41:43, speaker Judge Tony Graf ruling from the bench after the recess. The map's quote is a character-for-character match to the file, with only the lead-in "All right. I want to address the objections before me, starting with" omitted: "Mr. Novak made a hearsay objection as it relates to Mr. McBride. The court agrees. It is hearsay. At the same time, I'm only going to consider Mr. McBride's statements to provide context for the things that Lance Twiggs says and for their effects on Lance Twiggs. As such, the hearsay objection as it relates to the statements of Mr. McBride in State's Exhibit 16 is overruled." The correction the map claims is real and material: the profile's reporting-derived wording at line 189 says the court "ruled McBride's own statements ... were hearsay and directed focus onto Twiggs' answers," which conceals that the objection was OVERRULED and the statements ADMITTED. I also read the surrounding rulings (02:42:23 relevance — reserved as to transcript pages 19–20; 02:45:18 Rule 403 — overruled, with a publication bar 32:55–35:48) to confirm the hearsay ruling was not later revisited in that block.
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: T1 — Judge Graf's ruling from the bench, day3.txt 02:41:43. Supported form: the court AGREED the statements were hearsay but OVERRULED the objection, admitting Mr. McBride's statements for the limited purposes of providing context for what Lance Twiggs said and showing their effect on him. The clause "and directed focus onto Twiggs' answers" must be struck — it misdescribes a limited-purpose admission as a redirection and omits the overruling entirely. Downstream consequence to carry: because McBride's recorded statements are in evidence only for context and effect, they cannot be cited anywhere in the file for the truth of what they assert.

q142_verdicts.claim: The April 20 interview was given under oath, in lieu of live preliminary-hearing testimony, with a Class A misdemeanor false-statement warning.
q142_verdicts.basis: The substance is fully carried; the word "verbatim" in the proposed marking is not. Opened day4.txt lines 815–846. All three clauses are present and, better than the map states, the oath was not merely proposed but ADMINISTERED and AFFIRMED: line 818 (Rev 02:11:04) "This meeting is to use your statement here instead of your testimony at a preliminary hearing. You understand that?"; line 826 (02:11:13) "...I need to place you under oath and also give you an admonition about false statements. Okay? First, you do solemnly swear or affirm..." → line 830 (02:11:32) "Lance Twiggs: Yes."; line 834 (02:11:33) "...may be presented to a magistrate or a judge in lieu of your sworn testimony at a preliminary examination. Any false statement you make and that you do not believe to be true may subject you to criminal punishment as a class A misdemeanor. Do you understand that?" → line 838 (02:11:56) "Yes." Sworn corroboration verified at day3.txt lines 2047–2091 (01:05:38–01:06:31), including "taken in lieu of him having to come and testify at the preliminary hearing" → Davis: "Yes, it was. Yes, he was." FOUR things the row gets wrong or omits. (1) The immunity sentence the row dates to 02:12:22 is at line 842, in the turn following the 02:11:56 label; 02:12:22 is Mr. Twiggs's "Mm-hmm." (2) That sentence is one of the McBride statements Graf ruled hearsay (row 5) — admitted only for context and effect — so it cannot carry the truth of the immunity grant. (3) "Verbatim" is not establishable: the words come from an uncertified Rev machine transcript of audio played in a courtroom, and Rev labels the speaker only "Speaker 4." (4) At line 906 (Rev ~02:13:37) the questioner says "I realized my mic was muted at the onset" and RE-ADMINISTERS the oath and the false-statement admonition — the file must not present a single clean administration. Also unrecorded in §7.1: line 842 adds an obstruction-of-justice warning alongside the Class A misdemeanor warning.
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: T1 for the SUBSTANCE — oath administered and affirmed on the recording, statement taken in lieu of live preliminary-hearing testimony, and a Class A misdemeanor false-statement warning given and acknowledged — resting on day4.txt 02:11:04–02:11:56 as played in open court AND independently on Davis's sworn testimony at day3.txt 01:05:38–01:06:31. Drop "verbatim from the recording as played": quote-level wording is uncertified-machine-transcript dependent and the on-recording speaker is Rev-labelled "Speaker 4" only. Add to §7.1: the admonitions were repeated after the questioner's microphone was found muted at the onset, and an obstruction-of-justice warning accompanied the Class A misdemeanor warning. Do not cite the 02:11:56 immunity sentence in support — it is hearsay admitted for context and effect only.

q142_verdicts.claim: The defence fought public airing and 'proposed extensive redactions.'
q142_verdicts.basis: Opened day3.txt directly. All figures found verbatim inside the Lauren Hunt block at 01:07:31: 'Monday at about 4:00 PM, defense counsel sent us a transcript that was prepared by defense, the defense team... It was about a 21-page transcript and their suggested redactions are approximately 11 pages of it. In total, redactions appear on 16 of the 21 pages.' Patterns '21-page', '21 page', 'suggested redactions', '16 of the 21', 'approximately 11 pages' all hit under BOTH the join and hyphen U+FFFE readings. Speaker check: the label reads Lauren Hunt and CONTENT confirms it (same turn: 'we would object procedurally', 'the state's position') — this is the prosecutor's proffer and argument to the court, NOT sworn testimony and NOT a court finding. Direction check found a contradiction the map omits: Richard Novak, day3 ~01:15:04–01:16:20, states twice 'It's only a 20 page transcript.' The defence-prepared transcript itself is not in this library's corpus, so nobody here has counted its pages.
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: T1 (day3.txt, prelim-hearing transcript, uncertified Rev machine transcript, read directly 2026-08-17) — RECORDING LAYER ONLY: 'Lauren Hunt for the State represented to the court (day3 01:07:31) that the defence transcript was "about a 21-page transcript," that proposed redactions were "approximately 11 pages of it," and that "redactions appear on 16 of the 21 pages."' The counts must NOT enter the analyst layer as established: they are one counsel's characterisation of a document not held by this project, and the page count is contested on the record — Novak, day3 ~01:16:20: 'It's only a 20 page transcript.' Note both figures; resolve neither.

q142_verdicts.claim: The state said it was taken 'essentially by surprise' by last-minute redaction demands, having disclosed the video to the defence in April.
q142_verdicts.basis: Opened day3.txt. Verbatim at the 01:08:48 block: 'My procedural objections to this are that this is essentially by surprise. We were already a day into the preliminary hearing. Defense counsel had been aware since at least April 28th, 2026 when the recorded 1102 of Mr. Twiggs was provided to them...' The map's ellipsis correctly bridges one sentence. The date is further sharpened in Hunt's immediately preceding turn (01:07:31): 'On April 28th, 2026, the Utah County Attorney's Office provided this recorded 1102 statement of Mr. Twiggs to defense counsel.' Pattern 'surprise' searched under both U+FFFE readings, 7 hits each, identical. Speaker inferred from content (prosecutor's own procedural objection), consistent with the label. Defence contest confirmed: Novak, day3 ~01:16:20, 'There's no surprise here.' Both-directions search also surfaced material the map did NOT bank — Hunt's own later partial concession, day3 01:31:16: 'to be fair, he did send me a transcript with proposed redactions Monday, I believe at about 4:00 PM. It was not accompanied by any objections that he actually had.'
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: T1, verbatim (day3.txt 01:08:48, uncertified Rev transcript read directly) — counsel's on-record argument, not testimony. Date sharpened to April 28, 2026, and the disclosing office named: the Utah County Attorney's Office (day3 01:07:31). The entry must carry BOTH sides: Novak's 'There's no surprise here' (~01:16:20) AND Hunt's concession at 01:31:16 that the transcript was in fact sent Monday ~4:00 PM, unaccompanied by stated objections.

q142_verdicts.claim: Kirk-family attorney Jeffrey Neiman argued for full unredacted publication ('No redactions…').
q142_verdicts.basis: Opened day3.txt. Self-ID verbatim at 03:14:29: 'Your Honor, Jeffrey Neiman on behalf of the Kirk family.' Cued by Graf at 03:14:21: 'Counsel, if you would like to state your name.' Argument verbatim at 03:14:45: 'The Kirk family believes strongly that if the evidence is being admitted in this preliminary hearing, it should be made public for the world to see. No redactions. This court has tools at its disposal to make sure the defendant receives a fair trial.' Patterns 'Neiman', 'No redactions', 'doubt and distrust' all hit under both U+FFFE readings. ONE LOCATOR ERROR IN THE MAP: the continuation the map quotes — 'To not be transparent here, to not be open, to not let the world see what happened will create doubt and distrust in the judicial system' — sits in the 03:15:08 block, not 03:14:45. Speaker corroborated independently of the Rev label: Novak at 03:15:45 refers to 'Ms. Kirk's position ... as well stated by her counsel', and Graf at 03:22:03 refers to 'the victim representative, Erika Kirk.'
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: T1, verbatim (day3.txt: self-ID 03:14:29; 'No redactions' 03:14:45; 'doubt and distrust' sentence 03:15:08 — fix the map's single-timestamp citation). Mark as the on-record statement of counsel for a non-party victim representative — recording layer, not evidence and not a finding.

q142_verdicts.claim: Defence attorney Richard Novak countered that 'the number one concern in this proceeding is Mr. Robinson's right to a fair trial.'
q142_verdicts.basis: Opened day3.txt. Verbatim at the 03:16:36 block: '...with all due respect to the Kirk family and with all due respect to the media, and with all due respect to the public, the number one concern in this proceeding is Mr. Robinson's right to a fair trial, which means a jury which has not been exposed before it's in this courtroom...' Pattern 'number one concern' hit identically under both U+FFFE readings. Speaker chain verified three ways rather than by label alone: Graf cues 'Mr. Novak? Your mic's muted' at 03:15:27; the turn opens under the label Richard Novak at 03:15:45; and the 03:16:36 block is an unlabelled continuation paragraph inside that same turn. Content is unambiguously defence argument ('our client's right to a fair trial' at 03:15:45; Graf then addresses him 'Mr. Novak' at 03:17:31). Label and content agree.
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: T1, verbatim (day3.txt 03:16:36, within Novak's turn opening 03:15:45, cued by Graf at 03:15:27; uncertified Rev transcript read directly). Mark explicitly as defence counsel's argument — not sworn testimony, not a court finding.

q142_verdicts.claim: 'So "16 minutes" understates the withheld material' — the §7.2 resolution counts only additions to the withheld set.
q142_verdicts.basis: Opened day4.txt and re-read §7.2 of the profile. Both un-redactions are in the record and neither appears in the profile. (1) Graf at 52:39: 'it's roughly just a few seconds after 15:39 on the video starting with, "Was he?" And ending at 16:46 with the last word, "Asking" ... I am ruling that that may be played and published through all mediums in the courtroom and via video.' (2) Graf at 56:49: 'the court finds from 33:27 starting at, "Okay," until just before 33:40. I'm sorry, up to 33:40 may be published.' Both carve OUT of previously ordered withheld blocks (6:57→20:29 and 32:55→35:47). Procedural posture the map omits: both were requested by the STATE (Ballard, 46:26–48:51); Novak opposed the second (49:44–51:46); Graf granted the first in full and the second ONLY IN PART, standing by the redaction of 32:55→33:27 (55:38). Patterns '15:39', '16:46', '33:27', '33:40', 'may be published', 'all mediums' all hit under both U+FFFE readings. ARITHMETIC CONSEQUENCE THE MAP DID NOT FOLLOW THROUGH: 16m24s + 14s (the two 7s cuts) − ≈64s − 13s ≈ 15m21s of audio withheld — below 16 minutes.
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: T1 — the profile's §7.2 must ADD both partial un-redactions (day4 52:39 and 56:49), naming the State as the movant and the second as granted only in part. Beyond the map: the headline sentence 'So "16 minutes" understates the withheld material' must be requalified, not merely supplemented. Netted, audio suppression falls to ≈15m20s (approximate — the first release begins 'roughly just a few seconds after 15:39'). The sentence holds ONLY if the 4m54s VIDEO-ONLY redaction (20:29→25:23) is counted, which suppressed picture and not sound; say so, or the claim is unsupported as written.

q142_verdicts.claim: 'Portions were shown audio-only or with blacked-out video; exhibits Twiggs was shown within the interview (the note, texts, Discord messages) were withheld from broadcast.'
q142_verdicts.basis: Opened day4.txt. Two of three quotes verbatim and correctly attributed; one locator wrong; the supporting cite points the wrong way. (a) Ms. Hunt, 02:09:53, verbatim: 'there are sometimes large gaps of just black, empty, silent space. When there are large gaps, we will fast forward.' Speaker confirmed by content (she reports making the court's edits, then examines Agent Davis). (b) The Graf 'exception' quote is verbatim BUT SITS AT 42:09, NOT '~00:43' — the map's locator is off by ~41 minutes. Read in full, it is SCOPED: 'I'm requesting video-only redaction between 20 minutes and 29 seconds, and 25 minutes and 23 seconds ... any video showing anything other than Mr. McBride and Lance Twiggs was to be redacted with the exception of the screenshots of the images pulled from the surveillance video and the FBI bulletin.' The caps in the map are added emphasis, not source. (c) The 02:54:13 StEx 16.2 ruling ('only in the gallery, not for distribution on electronic media') CORROBORATES the profile's 'withheld from broadcast' for the Discord chats — it is not an exception. Same for 16.3, the photograph of notes: Graf, 03:01:18, 'may be published only in the courtroom and not be shown or videoed.' The counter-example the map MISSED is StEx 16.1, the text messages: Graf at ~01:28:39, 'because it was publicly distributed by the state, that 16.1 in its entirety may be broadcast through electronic media' (one page ordered redacted for containing contact details), and at 02:40:38, 'may be published to the gallery as well as electronically distributed through the camera.' All patterns run under both U+FFFE readings.
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: T1, with the exception SCOPED and the locator corrected: within the court's video-only redaction window 20:29→25:23, everything on screen other than the two interview participants was blacked out EXCEPT the surveillance-video screenshots and the FBI bulletin (Graf, day4 42:09 — not ~00:43). Drop StEx 16.2 from the exception: it supports the profile (day4 02:54:13, gallery only, no electronic distribution), as does 16.3 (day4 03:01:18, courtroom only, not to be videoed). Add instead the distinction the profile's sentence currently blurs: as STANDALONE exhibits the text messages (16.1) were NOT withheld — Graf ruled 16.1 broadcastable in its entirety through electronic media (day4 ~01:28:39, 02:40:38), minus one page redacted for contact details. The profile's parenthetical '(the note, texts, Discord messages)' is defensible only as a statement about the blackout WITHIN the played recording, and must say so.

q142_verdicts.claim: Graf stated he would privately review the full unredacted recording in making the probable-cause determination.
q142_verdicts.basis: I opened ~/Documents/Kirk Robinson Research/files - Court record/CR-ACQ-2026-07-27_court-record-artifacts/prelim-hearing-transcripts/day3.txt and .../day4.txt (both verified: no NUL bytes, no U+FFFE). CONFIRMED VERBATIM, day3.txt line 2395, continuation stamp 02:43:44 inside the turn opened at line 2372 'Judge Tony Graf (02:41:04)': 'After this hearing, my intent is to review everything again to be thorough. This is not a case where I'm going to be shooting from the hip and making that determination because this is an important determination.' CONFIRMED VERBATIM, day3.txt line 2659, stamp 03:10:05 inside the Graf turn at line 2652 (03:09:45): '...which the court will do again, because this is not something you do watch once and then make your decision. This requires analysis, and the Court is committed to doing that.' CONFIRMED VERBATIM, day4.txt line 522, 'Judge Tony F Graf Jr (55:38)': 'as previously stated, the entirety of Exhibit 16 the court is receiving without any redactions or edits. The court is considering it as it weighs probable cause.' Speaker inferred from content per standing hazard 9, not from Rev labels: the day3 turn contains 'As I am acting as a magistrate', 'I'm ordering that the audio cannot be published', and the day4 turn contains 'the court stands by its original ruling'. Also found, unprompted and supporting: day3.txt line 2639 (03:06:02) 'The Court is considering the entirety of State's Exhibit 16'. NARROWING — the word 'privately' is nowhere in either transcript. I ran artifact_search.find (both the join and hyphen U+FFFE readings) for the stem 'privat': day3 = 4 hits, all unrelated (privileged/private discussions in the decorum order; 'that doesn't make it private' about sidebar white noise); day4 = 0. 'in camera' = 0 in both. 'chamber' = 0 in day3 and 12 in day4, every one a firearm chamber in Sgt. Faumuina's testimony. The stems are capable of matching the thing claimed absent. Separately I checked day3's two 'unredact' hits: the one at 56:05 ('What I have is the unredacted version. So I want to review it before I make that decision') is about State's Exhibit 14, NOT Exhibit 16 — it must not be pressed into service for this row.
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: T1 — day3.txt 02:43:44, 03:06:02 and 03:10:05; day4.txt 55:38. Access caveat: uncertified Rev machine transcript of the courtroom feed. Scope: State's Exhibit 16, the April 20, 2026 recording, only. The word 'privately' is this project's (and the T3 outlets') characterization, not the court's; supported form: 'The court stated on the record that it receives and is considering Exhibit 16 in its entirety, without any redactions or edits, as it weighs probable cause, and that after the hearing it would review everything again — "this is not something you do watch once and then make your decision."' If 'privately' is kept, mark it as inference from the fact that the publication-barred portions played in the courtroom only as silent black gaps.

q142_verdicts.claim: Redactions at this stage do not control trial admissibility.
q142_verdicts.basis: CONFIRMED VERBATIM, day3.txt line 2403, continuation stamp 02:44:46 inside the Graf turn at line 2372: 'Even so, there are portions of this transcript, and again State's Exhibit 16, that may not be admissible at trial and whose relevance I have not yet determined.' The map's rendering matches the source exactly. Speaker confirmed from content — the same turn reads 'As I am acting as a magistrate, I do not have the same concerns... Therefore, for purposes of admissibility, the defendant's objection is overruled.' THE DAY 4 QUOTE IS MISQUOTED AND MIS-SCOPED. I found it at day4.txt line 734, inside the Graf ruling turn opened at line 719 (01:25:19). The court did not say 'relates only to'. It said: 'This ruling is limited to publication of the exhibits during the preliminary hearing and does not determine their admissibility at trial. And, I insert, if one occurs, or foreclose any later request for relief based on a more developed record.' More importantly, the subject of that ruling is stated four lines earlier at line 722: 'This matter comes before the court on state's request to publish exhibit 16.1, 16.2, and 16.3... The exhibits consist of text messages between Mr. Robinson and a witness, Discord messages between Mr. Robinson and others, and a written note the state attributes to Mr. Robinson.' It is NOT the ruling on Exhibit 16, the April 20 recording. The map's bare label 'day4 (the court's ruling)' would attach it to the recording, which the record does not support.
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: T1 — but split by source and scope. For the April 20 recording (Exhibit 16): cite day3.txt 02:44:46 only. For the documentary exhibits (16.1 text messages / 16.2 Discord messages / 16.3 the note): cite day4.txt 01:28:39 with its actual wording, 'This ruling is limited to publication of the exhibits during the preliminary hearing and does not determine their admissibility at trial... or foreclose any later request for relief based on a more developed record.' Do not present the day4 sentence as spoken about the recording. Access caveat: uncertified Rev machine transcript.

q142_verdicts.claim: Graf denied Neiman's parallel demand that all admitted exhibits be displayed in real time to everyone in the courtroom.
q142_verdicts.basis: CONFIRMED VERBATIM, day4.txt line 302 (continuation stamp 36:03) inside the Graf turn opened at line 295 (35:12): 'The court has considered the request that exhibits be displayed in real time to the courtroom. After careful consideration, the court determines that not all exhibits will be visually displayed to the gallery and notes that it will use a tiered method as described. First, whether it will be admitted to the court for consideration as it relates to probable cause. Second, whether it will be displayed only to the gallery. And third, if it will be published through the camera to the public at large.' The three-tier mechanism is verbatim. CONFIRMED VERBATIM, day4.txt line 306 (stamp 36:57): 'Transparency is an important principle, but it must be maintained in a manner consistent with the constitutional rights and protections afforded to all parties. The court does not make a blanket ruling as it relates to any exhibit.' Both sentences match the profile and the map exactly. THREE NARROWINGS. (1) 'followed verbatim by' is wrong as to contiguity: the Transparency sentence sits at 36:57, roughly 54 seconds and four intervening sentences after the '...displayed to the gallery' sentence at 36:03 (the intervening text runs 'This ruling is not intended to diminish the significance of the victim's representative rights... The manner in which evidence is displayed remains in the court's discretion...'). Applying the row as written would stitch two separated passages into one quotation. (2) Attribution: the court identified the movant only as 'Ms. Erika Kirk's attorney' (line 246) and 'the attorney for victim representative Erika Kirk'. Neiman is named as that attorney elsewhere on the same day — line 714, Graf: 'Ms. Kirk's victim representative attorney', answered by 'Jeffrey Neiman' at line 715; and line 642, 'Jeffrey Neiman on behalf of the Kirk family'. The attribution holds, but by that route, not because the ruling names him. (3) Direction: 'denied' overstates. The court refused a BLANKET order — 'The court does not make a blanket ruling as it relates to any exhibit... each exhibit will be afforded its own due' — and the same morning it GRANTED the relief in substance for the exhibits then at issue: line 734, 'the state may publish Exhibits 16.1, 16.2, and 16.3', with 16.1 'in its entirety may be broadcast through electronic media' subject to one redaction of a phone number and address. Neiman's own oral request, day4.txt line 642 (01:15:25), was that 'the evidence be displayed openly in this courtroom' for the family to see — a gallery-display request, not the categorical formulation the profile puts in his mouth.
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: T1, verbatim — with the two quoted sentences presented as separate passages of one continuous ruling (day4.txt 36:03 and 36:57), the movant described as the victim representative's counsel (Neiman, identified as such at day4.txt 01:24:38–01:24:57), and the holding stated as a refusal of a blanket/categorical order in favour of an exhibit-by-exhibit tiered method — not as a denial of courtroom display, which the court granted for Exhibits 16.1–16.3 later the same morning. Access caveat: uncertified Rev machine transcript.

q142_verdicts.claim: Twiggs said he never heard Robinson talk about Charlie Kirk before the shooting.
q142_verdicts.basis: CONFIRMED VERBATIM in day4.txt. Question, line 1454 (stamp 02:30:51): 'How about Charlie Kirk? Did he ever talk about Charlie Kirk?' Answer, line 1458 (stamp 02:30:54): 'I personally had never heard him talk about Charlie Kirk before specifically.' Both match the map character for character. Capacity established from inside the artifact, not assumed: the whole passage sits in the Rev block labelled 'Video (02:16:00)' at line 1027, opened at line 815 'Video (02:11:04)' immediately after Ms. Hunt moved 'to publish on the monitors State's Exhibit 16' (line 810), and closed by Graf at line 1519 (02:33:59) 'All right. That concludes state's exhibit 16.' Sworn status is established WITHIN the exhibit rather than inherited from the T3 outlets §7.1 relies on: line 818, 'This meeting is to use your statement here instead of your testimony at a preliminary hearing'; line 826, the oath administered in full, answered 'Yes' at line 830; line 834, the false-statement admonition and the notice that the statement 'may be presented to a magistrate or a judge in lieu of your sworn testimony at a preliminary examination', answered 'Yes' at line 838; line 842, acknowledgement of 'a federal agreement and a state agreement granting you immunity from prosecution', answered at line 846. That is an independent T1 confirmation of §7.1's oath / in-lieu-of-testimony / dual-immunity facts, logged here explicitly. Questioner: I did not rely on Rev's inline 'Speaker 2'/'Speaker 4' labels. The court and counsel identify the interviewer in Exhibit 16 on the record as Mr. McBride — day3.txt line 2383 (Graf: 'I'm only going to consider Mr. McBride's statements to provide context for the things that Lance Twiggs says') and day4.txt line 506 (Ballard: 'Right after 32:55 where Mr. McBride states, "Okay."'). A second voice, Rev's 'Speaker 6', is also present in the room, so I do not claim every question is his. Verification in both directions: I scanned the entire playback block, day4.txt lines 815–1518, for Charlie|Kirk|politic|Trump|gender|LGBT. The only hits are lines 874, 1446, 1450, 1454, 1458, 1462, 1466 — nothing in the published recording cuts against the answer. Absence scope: 16m24s plus three further Day-4 cuts were barred from publication and are therefore not in this transcript, so this is not a search of the whole recording.
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: T1 — State's Exhibit 16 as published in open court, day4.txt 02:30:51–02:30:54; sworn, under state and federal use immunity, per the oath and admonitions at day4.txt 02:11:04–02:12:22 inside the exhibit itself. Access caveat: uncertified Rev machine transcript of the courtroom audio of a played video. Quote the answer with its qualifiers intact — 'I personally had never heard him talk about Charlie Kirk before specifically' — and do not compress it to a flat 'never heard Robinson talk about Charlie Kirk'.

q142_verdicts.claim: They 'rarely discussed politics'; when they did it centred on Trump and current events.
q142_verdicts.basis: CONFIRMED VERBATIM, day4.txt line 1450 (stamp 02:30:23), answering the question at line 1446 (02:30:19) 'Did you and he ever talk about politics?': 'He did more than me. I still don't really keep up with politics very much. He'd usually talk about stuff he heard on the radio on his drive to work in their work car since it sounds like their whole crew went in the same car most of the time, but I wouldn't say super consistently because it wasn't a topic I really contributed much on.' The map's ellipsis correctly elides the work-car clause. The map's direction correction is RIGHT and I log it as confirmed: the source is asymmetric — Robinson raised politics, Twiggs did not engage — and 'They rarely discussed politics' flattens that into a symmetric proposition the witness did not state. THREE FURTHER NARROWINGS THE MAP DOES NOT STATE. (1) The 02:31:12 sentence is not a free-standing answer about politics. Line 1466 in full reads: 'No, not really. Usually, if he did talk about politics stuff, it was relating to Trump or current policies being issued or voted on, I think, but yeah.' That is the answer to the gender-identity/LGBTQ question at line 1462 (02:30:59). Rows 5 and 6 of this map are quarrying ONE answer turn without saying so, and the map's version silently drops the leading 'No, not really.' (2) The source says 'current policies being issued or voted on' — not 'current events'. The profile's wording is not what the witness said. (3) The witness hedges: 'I think, but yeah'.
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: T1 — day4.txt 02:30:23 and 02:31:12, State's Exhibit 16 as published; access caveat, uncertified Rev machine transcript. Restate as the asymmetry the source carries: asked whether he and Robinson ever talked about politics, Twiggs said Robinson 'did more than me', that he himself does not 'really keep up with politics very much', and that Robinson would relay radio content from his drive to work 'but I wouldn't say super consistently because it wasn't a topic I really contributed much on.' Replace 'current events' with 'current policies being issued or voted on', keep the 'I think' hedge, and attribute that sentence to the 02:31:12 answer — i.e. to the gender-identity question, not to a separate politics question.

q142_verdicts.claim: Robinson 'did not discuss gender identity or LGBTQ+ issues with him.'
q142_verdicts.basis: CONFIRMED VERBATIM, day4.txt line 1462 (stamp 02:30:59): 'Okay. How about political issues? So did you ever talk about gender identity issues and LGBTQ rights?' and line 1466 (stamp 02:31:12): 'No, not really.' The map's core point holds and I confirm it: the profile's form makes ROBINSON the subject and asserts something about a capital defendant's conduct — that he did not discuss these issues with Twiggs — which is neither what was asked nor what was answered. The question is addressed to 'you', and the answer is hedged, not absolute. BUT THE MAP'S OWN GLOSS OVERREACHES IN TURN. It renders the question as 'did YOU ever talk about' with emphasis and calls the question 'mutual, not one-directional'. There is no emphasis in the transcript, and 'you' is not disambiguated: it may be singular (Twiggs alone) or the plural 'you [and he]'. The preceding question at line 1446 was expressly 'Did you and he ever talk about politics?', which makes the plural reading plausible — but plausible is not established, and substituting 'mutual' for the ambiguity would repeat the error the row is correcting, in the other direction. LIVING-PERSONS FLAG CONFIRMED AND HONOURED: the immediately following exchange, day4.txt lines 1470–1482 (02:31:29–02:32:01), concerns the witness's personal identity and a name he has used. It bears on no public question in this file, it is about a private individual charged with nothing, and I have not reproduced it here. The map is right to mark it keep-out.
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: T1 — day4.txt 02:30:59–02:31:12, State's Exhibit 16 as published; access caveat, uncertified Rev machine transcript. Supported form: asked 'How about political issues? So did you ever talk about gender identity issues and LGBTQ rights?', Twiggs answered 'No, not really.' Drop the Robinson-as-subject framing entirely. Do not assert the question was 'mutual' — say that the question as transcribed is addressed to 'you' and that the transcript does not resolve whether that is Twiggs alone or Twiggs and Robinson. Keep the 02:31:29–02:32:01 exchange out.

q142_verdicts.claim: About a month before the shooting Robinson asked to borrow a Dremel to engrave bullets, describing a planned hunting trip with his family.
q142_verdicts.basis: Opened day4.txt directly. All four quoted strings are verbatim-accurate at 02:18:32, 02:19:06, 02:19:24 and 02:33:31. But the CAPACITY the map assumed is wrong in a way it never states: these are not live preliminary-hearing testimony. day4.txt 02:10:29–02:33:59 is the playback of State's Exhibit 16, a recorded statement; the oath colloquy at 02:11:04 reads 'This meeting is to use your statement here instead of your testimony at a preliminary hearing... I need to place you under oath', the interviewer closes at 02:33:34 with 'end the recording for the 11:02 purposes' (a Rev garble of '1102' — MARKED normalisation; 'Utah Rule of Evidence 1102' appears 31x in day3.txt and Graf invokes it by name in day4.txt at 05:19), and Graf then says 'That concludes state's exhibit 16.' I counted every 'Lance Twiggs' speaker line across day1–day5: 83, all of them inside the day4 byte range 53967–72166, i.e. entirely inside the exhibit. Twiggs never took the stand and was never cross-examined. The map also mis-anchors the key answer: 'at most a month' is at 02:19:24; 02:19:21 is the questioner's leading 'Are we talking a year before?'. Corroboration found and logged: Sgt. Faumuina, live sworn, day4.txt 05:01:00, lists 'a Dremel tool and its bits container' among items seized from the shared residence.
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: T1 — but as a SWORN RECORDED STATEMENT admitted as State's Exhibit 16 under Utah R. Evid. 1102 (reliable hearsay at preliminary examination) and published on day 4 (2026-07-09), NOT live cross-examined testimony. Mark: 'T1 (Twiggs sworn statement, State's Ex. 16, day4.txt 02:11:04–02:33:34, admitted under Utah R. Evid. 1102; declarant not cross-examined).' The 'about a month' figure must be recorded as an ELICITED UPPER BOUND: unprompted, Twiggs said 'I don't remember, because he'd been talking about the hunting/camping trip for a couple months' (02:19:06); 'It would've been, I'd say at most a month before' came only after the questioner's leading 'Are we talking a year before?' (question 02:19:21, answer 02:19:24). Also correct the verb: the profile says Robinson 'asked to borrow' the Dremel; the record is 'he asked me if we had a Dremel' and 'I just told him where it was' (02:33:31) — Twiggs did not hand it over. Add corroboration at true live-testimony T1: Faumuina, day4.txt 05:01:00.

q142_verdicts.claim: Shown surveillance photos, Twiggs said he 'couldn't be 100% certain' but they appeared to be Robinson.
q142_verdicts.basis: Opened day4.txt at 02:28:23 and 02:28:52. The transcript strings the map quotes are verbatim-accurate. But the profile's own quotation is not: line 210 of lance-twiggs-comprehensive-profile.md puts "couldn't be 100% certain" inside quotation marks, and Twiggs' actual words are 'I wouldn't say with 100% certainty just because of camera quality.' Stamping the row 'T1, verbatim' as the file currently reads would certify a misquote at Tier 1. Same Rule 1102 capacity finding as the Dremel row — this exchange sits inside the same State's Exhibit 16 playback, not live testimony. Direction check on 'surveillance photos': supported and independently corroborated — the questioner is on the FBI's website press release showing 'two rows of three images' (02:27:48), the Information (2025-09-16, 'The Washington County Investigation' section) says police 'published photos of the shooter from the UVU surveillance cameras', and Patel states in the 09-12 capture presser that 'At my direction, the FBI released the first set of FBI photos of the suspect at 10:00 AM local time on 9/11' — which matches Twiggs' 'I did the next day. I don't think I saw any on the 10th' (02:27:44).
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: T1 available for the SUBSTANCE, but the 'verbatim' label cannot be applied until the file's quotation is fixed. Mark: 'T1 (State's Ex. 16, day4.txt 02:28:23 and 02:28:52, sworn statement admitted under Utah R. Evid. 1102; declarant not cross-examined)' AND replace "couldn't be 100% certain" with the actual words, 'I wouldn't say with 100% certainty just because of camera quality.' Record the identification as partial and feature-based rather than global: he cited the shoes and sunglasses, said he had not specifically seen Robinson in that hat, said 'especially the bottom, the last two definitely do look like him', and answered 'Who's he?' with 'They do look like Tyler Robinson.'

q142_verdicts.claim: Courtroom observers reported Robinson furrowed his brow and smirked when the engraved-bullet messages were displayed; his mother cried as Discord messages were read.
q142_verdicts.basis: Re-ran the null myself with artifact_search.find over day1–day5, both U+FFFE readings. Capable patterns: 'smirk' (a stem that matches smirk/smirked/smirking) = 0 in all five files, both readings; 'furrow' = 0 in all five, both readings. The null holds. Two of the map's supports do not. (1) Its 'cried|crying|wept 2 hits — both in day4 and both Twiggs describing ROBINSON crying' is wrong on half: I opened both. One is Twiggs at day4 02:26:16 ('He started crying a little bit and said he wishes he hadn't done it'); the other is the substring 'wept' inside 'swept' in a quoted Robinson text ('I think they already swept that spot'). The map counted a substring artifact instead of opening it. I also ran 'mother|mom' — 0 hits in day4 entirely, and the one 'brow' hit in day1 is the surname 'Brown'. (2) The row's claim text says 'his mother cried as Discord messages were read'; I grepped the profile — that clause does not exist in it. §7.3 line 212 carries only the furrowed-brow-and-smirk sentence. The map is describing a claim the file does not make.
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: UNCHANGED (T3), observer layer — but the marking instruction must carry the null's SCOPE, or it reads as a finding it is not. Required form: 'Observation, not evidence (AP/The Hill). The five-day Rev transcript record does not contain it — "smirk" and "furrow" both return zero across day1–day5 under both U+FFFE readings — but a transcript of proceedings records speech, not demeanour, so this is not a search space that would necessarily contain a facial expression. The null therefore neither corroborates nor refutes the observation.' Do NOT import the 'his mother cried' clause into §7.3; it is not in the file and is not in the transcripts. Correct the pass's own note: only one of the two day4 crying hits is Twiggs describing Robinson (02:26:16) — and that line is itself upgradable to T1, since §3.5 line 113 currently cites it to Fox News liveblog/AP.

q142_verdicts.claim: Gov. Spencer Cox: conservative family, ideology 'very different than his family'; boyfriend transitioning male to female; 'very cooperative'; 'had no idea that this was happening.'
q142_verdicts.basis: Opened and searched all four held Rev official-statement transcripts myself, both U+FFFE readings, with patterns capable of matching each sub-claim: 'no idea' = 0, 'ideolog' = 0, 'platonic' = 0, 'male to female' = 0, 'Twigg' = 0 across all four. I chased every near-miss rather than trusting the counts. 'very cooperative' has exactly one hit — the 09-10 presser praising 'the local police department, and the university police department, all of which have been very cooperative' — agencies, not Twiggs. 'very different'/'different than' produce three hits, all false leads: Cox on political violence being 'different than any other type of violence', Cox on building a culture 'very different than what we are suffering through', and the Gray presser on Robinson and his father having 'very different political views'. In the 09-12 capture presser a reporter does ask 'Is he cooperative with authorities?' (26:54) — about Robinson, and Cox deflects without answering. None of the four Cox sub-claims is in the held primary record. Folder-wide sweeps were never used; every search named its files explicitly, so the mis-banked BAM Franchising artifact was out of scope by construction.
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: UNCHANGED — mark 'T2 via T3' (Cox's television interviews, held in this library only through reporting). One ADDITION is required so the file does not imply the primary corpus is silent on the underlying proposition: the transitioning sub-claim IS separately carried at T1. The sworn Information of 2025-09-16 records Robinson's mother's statement to police that Robinson 'began to date his roommate, a biological male who was transitioning genders', and Gray recites the same at the 09-16 charging press conference (~17:5x). That is a family member's police statement recorded in a charging instrument — attributed, not adopted, not an official finding, and not Cox. The map's 'transgender|transition 0' is true only of the Cox/Patel capture presser; the Gray presser returns three hits.

q142_verdicts.claim: FBI Deputy Director Dan Bongino confirmed the name and cited 'a good body of information' indicating a beyond-platonic relationship.
q142_verdicts.basis: Searched all four held Rev transcripts, both readings. 'Bongino' returns exactly one hit in the entire held record, and I opened it and read 3,000 characters of surrounding context rather than accepting the label. The line is 'Myself and Deputy Director Bongino arrived on scene at approximately 5:30 PM' — a third-person mention inside a timeline narration, not Bongino speaking. Speaker inferred from CONTENT per standing hazard 9, not from the Rev label: the same turn says 'At my direction, the FBI released the first set of FBI photos of the suspect', thanks President Trump on behalf of the FBI, and addresses 'Governor Cox' as a counterpart — that is the FBI Director, Kash Patel, and the Rev label agrees. Bongino never speaks anywhere in the held record. The null the row rests on holds with capable patterns: 'platonic' = 0, 'good body' = 0, 'body of information' = 0, across all four files under both readings.
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: UNCHANGED — mark 'T2 via T3'. The held primary record contains no Bongino statement at all; his only appearance is as the object of Patel's sentence. The 'good body of information' / beyond-platonic remark is an individual official's podcast remark known to this library only through reporting, and must never be promoted. Recommended note in §8.3: 'Bongino does not speak in any held primary transcript; his single appearance in the record is Patel's timeline narration placing him on scene at approximately 5:30 PM on 09-11 (fbi-captures-kirk-shooter.txt, ~08:5x).'

q142_verdicts.claim: Utah County Attorney Jeff Gray built the charging narrative around the texts Twiggs preserved.
q142_verdicts.basis: Opened both named artifacts. T2 primary layer confirmed verbatim: Gray's 09-16 presser at ~04:36 reads 'Count five, witness tampering, a third degree felony for directing his roommate to delete his incriminating texts. Count six, witness tampering, a third degree felony for directing his roommate to stay silent if police questioned him.' T1 layer confirmed by reading the Information rather than accepting the map's paraphrase (the map supplied no verbatim string for it): the document reproduces the Robinson–roommate text exchange at length, and Counts 5 and 6 recite it expressly — Count 5 'directing his roommate to delete incriminating text messages', Count 6 quoting 'if any police ask you questions ask for a lawyer and stay silent'. The instrument is sworn ('Sworn to by: JEFFREY S. GRAY, Utah County Attorney'). Three direction problems the map did not catch. First, 'Twigg' returns ZERO in the Information — he is 'his roommate' throughout, so a T1 stamp cannot carry a named identification. Second, 'built the charging narrative around the texts' overstates the document: the texts are one section of a seven-count probable-cause statement whose murder counts rest on the shooting, DNA consistent with Robinson on the trigger, the concealed rifle, the discarded clothing, the parents' and family friend's statements and the residence search. Third, 'preserved' is the profile's word; the Information says the roommate 'received messages from Robinson about the shooting and provided those messages to police.'
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: Both tiers are carried, but the sentence must be narrowed before either is stamped. Mark: 'T1 (Information, 2025-09-16, sworn by Jeffrey S. Gray — Counts 5 and 6 and the reproduced text exchange they rest on) / T2 primary (Gray's 09-16 charging press conference, held transcript, ~04:36).' Rewrite the claim as: 'Counts 5 and 6 of the Information are built on the Robinson–roommate text exchange, which the roommate provided to police; the Information reproduces that exchange and does not name him, referring throughout to "his roommate." The remaining counts rest on other evidence.' Do not carry 'built the charging narrative around' or 'preserved' into an upgraded tier.

q142_verdicts.claim: Gray declined to endorse identity-based motive framing.
q142_verdicts.basis: Opened .../2026-08-16_rev_update-on-charlie-kirk-shooter.txt in full (392 lines). artifact_search.audit: 0 NUL, 0 U+FFFE — so both readings are identical for this file; I ran find() which checks both anyway. 34:07 CONFIRMED verbatim; questioner self-identifies 'Mr. Gray, [inaudible 00:34:09] with Fox News' (Rev label 'Speaker 2' — attribution rests on the self-ID in content, not the label). 34:17 IS A MISQUOTE: Gray actually says 'I'm going to stick to what I just stated in my public… In our information. I think that is pretty much set forth there.' — NOT 'what I just said.' Material difference: Gray refers the questioner TO the filed Information, he does not flatly refuse. 35:42 CONFIRMED verbatim (BBC's 'Dennis'), but the map drops the material first clause 'The governor previously said the roommate is cooperating, but…'. 37:58 answer CONFIRMED verbatim; the map's GLOSS is wrong — Carter Evans (CBS) asked 'are you confident that the roommate had no part of this attack whatsoever?' (about Gray's confidence), not what the evidence showed; 'does it show any involvement' is a separate question at 38:00. The profile's existing text already renders this correctly; the map degrades it. BOTH DIRECTIONS — logged against the upgrade: in this same T2 primary Gray himself puts identity-adjacent content on the record (PC recital that Robinson 'began to date his roommate, a biological male who was transitioning genders' and had become 'more pro-gay and trans rights oriented'; and that Kirk 'was answering a question about mass shootings by transgender individuals when a gunshot rang out').
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: T2 — named official's own words at his own press conference, read directly — WITH a Rev machine-transcript caveat (uncertified; timestamps are Rev stream offsets, ±~5 min, never clock times). NOT 'verbatim' as proposed: the map's 34:17 Gray quote must not be pasted into the file. Restate the claim narrowly: asked whether transgender issues played a role in the motivations, Gray deflected to the filed Information rather than affirming or denying — 'I'm going to stick to what I just stated in my public… In our information. I think that is pretty much set forth there.' Drop 'stronger than the profile states': Gray did not disavow identity framing, he deferred to a charging document whose pleaded aggravator is political expression.

q142_verdicts.claim: As of September 2025 the FBI had issued no institutional statement about Twiggs' personal relationships.
q142_verdicts.basis: Opened all three transcripts. audit: 0 NUL / 0 U+FFFE in each; all patterns run through artifact_search.find, i.e. under both readings, and I say so. CAPABLE surname pattern used: r'Twi\w{0,6}' (matches Twiggs/Twigg/Twigs/Twix and any Rev garble on that stem) — ZERO across all three. r'\bLance\b' — ZERO (the four raw 'Lance' substring hits in the 09-12 file are both 'surveillance', opened and read). r'boyfriend' / r'romantic' / r'dating|dated' / r'transgender' / r'gender' / r'intimate' — zero personal-relationship characterisations anywhere; the sole 'relationship' hit is Patel on 'no better relationship for law enforcement than the FBI to partner with state and local authorities'. So the NULL IS CONFIRMED and well-founded. Speakers verified: FBI SAC Robert Bohls speaks at 09-10; an FBI speaker (unnamed in Rev labels) at 09-11; Director Patel at 09-12 — FBI officials do speak at all three. TWO OVER-CLAIMS: (1) the 09-12 presser does NOT refer 'only to "the roommate of Robinson"' — I opened every hit; it uses 'the roommate of Robinson', 'that roommate', 'his roommate', 'Robinson's roommate', 'Robinson's roommate's device'. The true finding is that he is referenced only by his roommate relation, never by name. (2) A press-conference remark by a named FBI official is a T2 named-official statement, not an FBI institutional statement/press release — so this null is adjacent to the §8.3 claim, it does not confirm it.
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: Sourced claim UNCHANGED at T3 (thenewsgrail.com). The new negative is an ANALYST-LAYER scoped finding resting on three T2 primaries — it is not itself 'at T2'; the tier belongs to the sources, not to the project's finding. Supported form: 'Across the three held Rev transcripts of the 2025-09-10, 09-11 and 09-12 official press conferences, no speaker named Lance Twiggs (capable stem Twi\w{0,6}: zero hits, both U+FFFE readings) and no speaker characterised any personal relationship between him and Robinson; the 09-12 presser identifies him only by his roommate relation to Robinson. Scope: these three transcripts only — not FBI press releases, written statements, or any press conference not held. Vehicle: uncertified Rev machine transcripts.' The Rev caveat the map demands for Row 5 must attach here too.

q142_verdicts.claim: The protective detail (never officially announced) reportedly ended by mid-January 2026; retired agent Jason Pack called this routine.
q142_verdicts.basis: NULL CONFIRMED, exactly as described. Ran r'protective detail', r'security detail', r'FBI protection', plus r'\bdetail\b', r'protect\w+', r'protective custody', r'threat[s]? (against|to)' over day1–day5 via find() (both U+FFFE readings; audit shows 0 NUL / 0 splits in these files). 'protective detail' and 'FBI protection': zero across all five. 'security detail': exactly one hit, day2 — I opened it: Agent Hull, examined by Mr. Sturgill, on Robinson's vehicle at Campus Drive/800 South making contact with Officer Goforth of Spanish Fork PD 'who was doing security detail'. Unrelated to Mr. Twiggs. The map's gloss of that hit is accurate. (day1's 'Mr. Kirk's detail, his own security team' is Kirk's own detail and does not match the phrase pattern.) Capable pattern claimed: 'security detail' — it demonstrably matched the only person-protection usage in the corpus. WHAT IS NOT TESTABLE: the Fox News article is NOT held on disk. The repo's only trace is the §12 URL in the profile itself. So 'the underlying source is anonymous / T4-within-T3' cannot be verified first-hand — the sole on-disk support is the URL slug '...-no-longer-under-fbi-protection-source-says', and a slug is metadata someone typed, not the article's content. Same for anything Pack said. FIRST-HAND DEFECT THE ROW MISSES: the profile sources this one fact three inconsistent ways — §8.1 'Unnamed relative (Fox News Digital, Jan. 15, 2026)'; §9 'Fox News — single law-enforcement source, tier 2/3 boundary'; §12 'relative's account'.
q142_verdicts.corrected_marking: T3 (Fox News, 2026-01-15), retrieval-date-stamped, and marked ⛔ NOT HELD ON DISK — not independently readable by this project. Do NOT write 'T4-sourced within a T3 vehicle' as an established marking; it is an inference from a URL slug. Write instead: 'underlying source not independently verified; the profile's own three sourcings of this fact conflict and must be reconciled before any tier is assigned.' Pack's characterisation is correctly an assessment, not a verification — but that note also rests on the unheld article and must be recorded at the recording layer only. q142_verdicts.claim: Twiggs went almost entirely dark publicly — social accounts locked or deleted; no interviews; no statements.

verdicts.reason:
A narrow core survives, but the finding's headline must be rejected — and on the living-persons lens the rejected part is the dangerous part.

WHAT SURVIVES (verified by capable patterns). The affidavit clause is verbatim at lines 114-118, and three things are genuinely not in the profile: the "made a joke on discord" statement, the screen-photography capture method, and any citation of the affidavit for either. Pattern "jok" over the profile returns exactly ONE hit — line 91, Twiggs' own quoted text "You're joking, right????" — so a pattern capable of matching "made a joke" was run and found nothing else. "screen" returns one hit (line 198, the §7.2 redaction timecodes); "photograph" returns two (lines 85, 266), neither describing investigators photographing his phone; "Cellebrite|RCFL|Larson|Ling|SIAC|extract|seiz" all return zero. §3.7's sentence "He handed over his phone contents: the text thread, the photo of the note, and Discord material" carries no citation at all, and its itemisation is wrong in one respect: the note photo was not handed over as an item.

WHAT IS REFUTED, ON PRIMARY SOURCES I OPENED MYSELF.
(1) "Rather than receiving his phone contents" is contradicted, not merely overstated. Davis, day3 01:02:53-01:03:17: Q "Do you know if his phone was taken from him?" A "It was… during that interview with FBI at St. George Police Department… he provided his phone. He did it voluntarily also, provided it to those agents." Day4 02:58:07: "following Lance's first interview at St. George PD, his phone is recovered at that point, taken into evidence… The FBI transported that phone to the RCFL… downloaded through Cellebrite… it went to a SIAC analyst… And at that point that this image of this letter was located." The screen photographs and the handover are sequential steps of one interview, not alternatives. Speakers inferred from content per standing hazard: the questioner lays foundation ("Are you familiar with an individual named Lance Twiggs?", "How do you know that?"); the answerer responds as case agent and concedes "No, I was not there" about the interview itself. Rev labels not relied on.
(2) "Entirely absent" is false on the profile's face — §3.4 (line 107) already records that "Twiggs showed investigators Discord messages attributed to Robinson discussing the rifle and engraved bullets."
(3) "The only Tier 1 account" is false — day3 and day4 are richer T1 records of the same interview (location, the two FBI agents by name, audio/video recording, exhibit provenance).
(4) The affidavit does NOT date the interview. Its only timestamps are the form's own arrest date/time field ("On 09/12/2025 04:00 the defendant was arrested", line 10, repeated at the signature) and the submission block's 09/12/2025 07:18. It yields a ceiling, not an anchor.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE RECORD THE EARLIER PASS WORKED FROM. The Information does not carry the "joke" clause — its single "jok" hit is Twiggs' own "You're joking, right????" at the text-thread reproduction — and "discord" returns 0 in the Information under BOTH the join and hyphen readings. And neither charging document names him: "\bTwigg" = 0 and "\bLance\b" = 0 in both documents under both readings (an unbounded "Lance" search returns 11 and 7 false hits respectively, all the substring inside "surveillance" — a false-positive trap worth recording).

SOURCE-INDEPENDENCE CALIBRATION. Gov. Cox's September 12 remarks reproduce the affidavit paragraph almost verbatim (2026-08-16_rev_fbi-captures-kirk-shooter.txt, 01:47-02:45; speaker established from content — the block opens "Good morning… We got him", runs unbroken to "I'll now turn the microphone over to the director of the FBI, Kash Patel", and Patel answers "Thank you, Governor"; an introducer names "Governor Cox, Director Patel and Commissioner Mason"). That is the same affiant text read aloud, so it is a T2 restatement, not independent corroboration. Do not count it as a second verification act.

MY LENS — LIVING PERSONS. Adopting the finding as written would put materially MORE about a man charged with nothing into the file, on a weaker basis, in the more damaging direction. Two specific harms. First, "his own characterisation of the Discord material as 'a joke'" converts a third-hand paraphrase into a quoted stance: the grammatical subject of "made a joke" is Robinson, the clause concerns one unidentified Discord item, and the affiant testified he was not present. Rendering it as Twiggs' characterisation of a body of evidence reads as minimisation and implies knowledge the source cannot carry — exactly the state-of-mind inference the project forbids. Second, glossing "as each message was shown by Robinson's roommate" as "he controlled what was displayed" imports gatekeeping that the sworn record contradicts, since the phone itself went into evidence and was fully extracted. The finding's preferred fix would have made §3.7 claim LESS cooperation than Tier 1 supports — the direction of error runs against him, which is the signal that flagged it.

Narrowed as below, the item adds one bounded recording-layer sentence and REMOVES an uncited, partly inaccurate itemisation. Net it puts less unsupported personal conduct in the file, not more, which is why it survives rather than being dropped.

RESIDUAL SCOPE. I did not re-verify the profile's AP/NewsNation/ABC4/CNN secondary citations, the April 20 2026 second-interview content, or the day5 "warrant" passages (8 hits) to establish whether any warrant or consent instrument governed retention of his phone after the voluntary handover — Davis's testimony is the only account of the taking I read. Counter-searches for material cutting against voluntary provision returned nothing in day1, day2, day5, the 2026-08-11 defence brief or the 2026-06-22 contempt hearing transcript ("voluntar", "warrant", "jok", "photograph.{0,20}(phone|screen)", "consent", both readings). The mis-banked BAM Franchising file (…utd-165286-1-4-1_dc28417731.txt) was never in scope: every search was aimed at named files, not a folder-wide sweep, so it contributed no hits.

(A) REPLACE §3.7's uncited sentence "He handed over his phone contents: the text thread, the photo of the note, and Discord material" with a two-step description that corrects the one real error without weakening the cooperation the record establishes:

"At the September 12, 2025 interview at St. George Police Department (FBI Agents Larson and Ling), Twiggs showed investigators messages on his phone and allowed them to be photographed as each was displayed; he then voluntarily provided the phone itself, which was taken into evidence and forensically downloaded. The text-thread and Discord exhibits (State's 16.1 and 16.2) are those photographs of his phone. The photo of Robinson's note (State's 16.3) was not handed over as a discrete item — a DPS SIAC analyst located it inside the forensic download."

(B) FIX THE TIER, NOT THE DATE, IN §3.7. The Sept. 12, 2025 date currently rests on AP (T3); it is confirmed at Tier 1 by Davis — "The first time was the early morning hours of September 12th, and that occurred at St. George Police Department" (day3 01:01:55). Replace the AP attribution; keep the date. Retain the existing note declining to anchor the interview to Robinson's booking.

(C) RECORD THE "JOKE" CLAUSE ONLY AT THE WIDTH THE SOURCE CARRIES, at the recording layer, in §3.4 alongside the existing Discord sourcing:

"The probable-cause affidavit records that investigators identified and interviewed Robinson's roommate, 'who stated that his roommate (referring to Robinson) made a joke on discord,' after which investigators asked if he would show them those messages. The subject of the remark is Robinson. The affidavit does not identify which message, does not report the roommate applying that word to Robinson's confession, the note or the text thread, and establishes nothing about what he knew or believed. The affiant was not present at the interview (Davis, day4 02:36:59: 'No, I was not there'), so this is a third-hand paraphrase, not a quotation of Mr. Twiggs — and the affidavit does not name him, referring throughout to 'the roommate.'"

Confidence: High as to the fact of the statement; the referent is unestablished. Do NOT render this as "his initial characterisation to police was a joke" or as a characterisation of the Discord material as a whole.

(D) UPGRADE §3.4's TIER. §3.4 currently sources "Twiggs showed investigators Discord messages" to CNN and AP/The Hill (T3). The same act is in the affidavit at T1 and in Davis's testimony at T1. Re-mark it; do not add new conduct.

(E) DO NOT ADOPT, and note expressly if the register entry is written up: §3.7's "handed over his phone contents" is supported in substance at Tier 1 and must not be narrowed to imply he withheld the phone or selected what investigators saw. The affidavit's "as each message was shown by Robinson's roommate" describes the sequence of display, not gatekeeping; the phone was voluntarily provided at that same interview and fully extracted.

(F) ATTRIBUTION CAUTION. Gov. Cox's September 12, 2025 remarks reproduce this affidavit paragraph almost verbatim. Cite the affidavit as the source (T1) and note the Cox reading as a T2 restatement of the same text — not as independent corroboration, and not as a second verification act.

(G) NAMING CAUTION for any future quotation from these two filings: neither names him ("\bTwigg" = 0, "\bLance\b" = 0, both documents, both readings). Render as "the roommate," not as if the filing named him.
