verdicts.reason:
REFUTED as framed. The quote is real and Cox is the right speaker — but the source does not say the thing the finding's headline says, in the sense it says it.

WHAT PASSES. The quoted words are verbatim at line 11 of the Cox/Patel transcript. Speaker inferred from CONTENT, not the Rev label: the block opens "Good morning ladies and gentlemen. We got him," is prepared first-person narration, later says "a terrible day for the state of Utah," and closes "I'll now turn the microphone over to the director of the FBI, Kash Patel," to which the next speaker replies "Thank you, Governor." Label and content agree. It is not a reporter's premise and not a Q&A answer. Date confirmed from content: Patel says the suspect was "taken into custody at 10 PM local time" last night and cites "33 hours" — the morning of 2025-09-12. The finder's ellipsis drops only "referring to Robinson" and "by Robinson's roommate"; neither alters sense.

WHY IT FAILS: THE SOURCE IS SILENT, NOT CONTRARY. "Contradict" requires the source to say something incompatible with "handed over his phone contents." Cox's narration stops at the screen photographs and never once addresses what became of the phone. Capable patterns over the whole 384-line file, run through artifact_search.find() so both the join and hyphen readings were tested (the file contains ZERO U+FFFE, so the two readings are byte-identical here): "turn(ed) over" = 0; "surrender(ed) his/the phone" = 0; "custody of his/the phone" = 0; "hand" = 1 unique hit, and it is "in all of our hands and in all of our pockets"; "provid" = 1 unique hit, and it is Patel's "provide them the evidence they need"; "gave" = 3 unique hits, all "you gave it to us" / "the timeline that Director Patel gave us"; "phone" = 4 unique hits, of which two are "microphone" and one is Cox's homily "Turn off your phone, read scripture," leaving exactly ONE substantive use — "the phone contact name Tyler with an emoji icon and Robinson's roommate's device." Patterns capable of matching a handover were run and returned nothing. Silence is not contradiction.

AND THE SILENCE IS EXPECTED, SO IT IS NOT PROBATIVE. Under the project's own rule, absence is evidence of absence only where the search space would necessarily contain the record. This one would not: it is a same-morning statement given hours after the interview, and before the extraction had even occurred (Davis, day4 02:58:07: the phone "is downloaded, I believe it was the following day or shortly after that"). Cox also refuses elaboration four times in the Q&A I read around the passage — "I cannot speak to that right now" (25:07), "There's nothing more that we can share at this time" (25:47), "I can't share any more than what I've already shared" (26:58–27:00), "I can't answer that right now" (27:51). A chain-of-custody detail was never going to be in this document.

"ACTUALLY" IS THE TELL. The finding says Cox describes how the messages "actually" reached investigators — asserting his account displaces §3.7's. It does not. I verified §3.7's substance at T1 by direct read, not from the banked map: day3 01:02:53–01:03:14, "Do you know if his phone was taken from him?" / "It was." / "he provided his phone. He did it voluntarily also, provided it to those agents," dated to September 12, 2025; and day4 02:37:42–02:37:48, "during that first interview on September 12th, physically, he shows them the phone and then allows them to photograph the phone" (photographs by FBI Agent Larson, 02:37:34). Speakers inferred from content — Hunt asks, Davis answers as case agent in first-person investigative narrative and disclaims personal knowledge where he lacks it ("I don't do that myself"; "I don't believe I specifically talked to those individuals"). The showing-and-photographing and the handover are SEQUENTIAL STEPS OF ONE INTERVIEW. Cox narrates step one. §3.7 compresses both.

THE "JOKE" LIMB IS A CATEGORY ERROR. It concerns why investigators asked to see Discord; it says nothing whatever about the mechanism of transfer, so it cannot contradict "handed over his phone contents." Bundling it into this finding is a non-sequitur regardless of its truth.

THE NOTE-PHOTO LIMB MISUSES COX. He never mentions the note in any form: "letter" = 0, "keyboard" = 0, "note" = 1 hit and it is the verb in "Investigators noted inscriptions." Offering him as a source that fails to support the note-photo claim is true only in the way any wholly silent document is.

THE BONUS OVER-READS. "Investigators identified an individual as the roommate of Robinson. Investigators interviewed that roommate" carries investigator-INITIATED contact and nothing more. It does not carry §3.6's relative-sourced "had to locate him and bring him in for questioning," which imports difficulty or reluctance — and Cox's very next sentence has him opening Discord and showing messages on request. §3.6's "not officially confirmed" marking should stand.

CONFIRMATIONS LOGGED (verifying in both directions). Cox's passage SUPPORTS the profile in three places and weakens it in none: (i) it corroborates at T2 §3.4's "Twiggs showed investigators Discord messages," currently carried at T3 on CNN/AP — a real tier upgrade is available; (ii) it corroborates at T2 that the photographed messages carried the rifle-from-a-drop-point, bush, towel, engraved-bullets and scope content; (iii) it corroborates investigator-initiated first contact. Nothing in the transcript cuts against §3.7.

DIRECTION-OF-ERROR (living persons). Adopting this finding would make the file claim LESS cooperation by a man accused of nothing than the sworn record supports — striking a T1-backed clause on the strength of a source silent on the point — while simultaneously imputing to him a minimising "joke" stance the source does not carry. Both limbs err against the same private individual.

RESIDUAL SCOPE. I did not re-verify §3.7's AP/NewsNation/ABC4 secondary citations, the April 2026 second interview, or whether any consent form or warrant governed retention of the phone after the voluntary provision — Davis's "he provided his phone... voluntarily" is the only sworn account of the taking that I read. I also did not resolve a separate issue this reading exposed and which is NOT part of this finding: Cox frames the request as one for DISCORD messages but then describes the resulting photos as messages with "the phone contact name Tyler" — i.e. the text thread — whereas day4 keeps Exhibits 16.1 (text) and 16.2 (Discord) distinct. That belongs to §3.4, not §3.7. Finally, a map hazard worth recording: the banked pass's profile line numbers have drifted against v1.3 — the "You're joking, right????" text is at line 91, not 95, and §3.4's "showed investigators" sentence is at line 107, not 111.

(a) COMPLETENESS, NOT CONTRADICTION — §3.7 compresses a three-step acquisition into one uncited clause. Tier 1 (Davis, day3 01:02:53–01:03:14; day4 02:37:34–02:38:03 and 02:58:07–02:59:05). Confidence: High. This ALSO fixes the one genuine wording defect in §3.7, which the finding never identified: the itemised list assigns Twiggs an affirmative act he did not perform — the photo of the note was not handed over as a discrete item, it was located by analyst search of the extraction. Confirmed absent from the profile by capable patterns: "Cellebrite", "RCFL", "SIAC", "Larson", "into evidence" all return 0; "photos of the screen" returns 0 and "screen" returns 1 hit (line 198, the redaction passage); "voluntar" returns 1 hit and it is the buccal swab, not the phone.

(b) A RECORDING-LAYER OMISSION, at the width the source carries and no wider — the profile nowhere records the statement that prompted investigators to ask for the Discord messages. Supported text: "Gov. Cox stated at the September 12, 2025 press conference (T2) — and the probable-cause affidavit records in near-identical words (T1) — that investigators interviewed Robinson's roommate, who stated that Robinson 'made a joke on Discord,' after which investigators asked if he would show them those messages." It is NOT a quotation of Mr. Twiggs; on its face it characterises what ROBINSON posted; it identifies no particular message; and it establishes nothing about how he regarded the confession, the note, the texts, or the Discord material as a whole. Do NOT render it as "his own characterisation" or "his initial framing to police was a joke." (c) Leave §3.6 unchanged. Cox's investigator-initiated phrasing does not corroborate the relative's stronger claim, and Davis's "he provided his phone... voluntarily" cuts the other way.

verdicts.reason:
REFUTED as framed. Under the materiality lens the difference is real but is additive detail plus one precision defect — not a contradiction — and the finding's central move fails for a reason neither prior lens stated.

1. IT IS NOT TWO ACCOUNTS. IT IS ONE DOCUMENT. I set Cox's line 11 beside the probable-cause affidavit and they are the same text, near-verbatim ("Investigators identified an individual as the roommate of Robinson. Investigators interviewed the roommate, who stated that his roommate (referring to Robinson) made a joke on discord..."). The affiant is "UTBDAVIS - Brian Davis," entered 09/12/2025 07:18. Cox was reading the PC affidavit aloud. So the finding sets "Cox's account" against a profile sentence whose Tier 1 support is sworn testimony by THE SAME MAN, Brian Davis. There is no rival narrator and no witness conflict to resolve. A finding titled "Cox's account contradicts X" that is really "Davis's 07:18 affidavit is shorter than Davis's later sworn testimony" is a difference dressed as a contradiction.

2. SILENCE, NOT CONTRADICTION — and the silence is exactly what the timeline predicts. Cox says nothing about a handover either way. Capable patterns run over the Cox file with artifact_search.find(), which tests BOTH the joined and hyphenated U+FFFE readings: 'hand' (2 hits, both "in all of our hands"), 'seiz' (2, forensic evidence generally, not the roommate), 'gave' (6, none on point), 'device' (2, same sentence), 'into evidence' 0, 'took his' 0, 'extract' 0, 'download' 0, 'Cellebrite' 0, 'search warrant' 0, 'subpoena' 0 — all null under both readings. Every literal "phone" in the file is "the phone contact name Tyler," two instances of "microphone," and a Kirk quotation "Turn off your phone." Nothing in Cox denies a handover. And the affidavit was entered at 07:18 on 09-12, hours after an early-morning interview and BEFORE the phone was downloaded ("I believe it was the following day or shortly after that," day4 02:58:07). A snapshot taken at t0 of a chain that continued is not an inconsistent account of the chain.

3. THE TWO EVENTS ARE SEQUENTIAL STEPS OF ONE INTERVIEW, BOTH TIER 1, AND I READ BOTH MYSELF. day3 01:02:53-01:03:14, Davis: Q "Do you know if his phone was taken from him?" A "It was." ... "So It was during that interview with FBI at St. George Police Department. They conducted an interview of him and then he provided his phone. He did it voluntarily also, provided it to those agents." day4 02:37:42-02:37:48, Davis: "during that first interview on September 12th, physically, he shows them the phone and then allows them to photograph the phone" (photos by FBI Agent Larson, 02:37:34). Speakers inferred from content per the standing hazard: Hunt asks, Davis answers in first person as case agent and says "No, I was not there" of the interview — Q-and-A structure, not labels. Cox narrates the showing; §3.7 compresses the showing AND the handover. The profile's clause is a superset of Cox's, not a rival to it.

4. THE "JOKE" LIMB CANNOT CONTRADICT A MECHANISM SENTENCE. It is not a mechanism claim at all. Bundling it under a heading about "handed over his phone contents" is a category error. It is separately real — 'jok' over the profile returns exactly one hit (line 95, Twiggs' own text "You're joking, right????"), so the pattern demonstrably matches "joke" and the affidavit statement is genuinely absent — but it belongs in its own item, at affidavit width, and it is Tier 1 in the affidavit before it is Tier 2 in Cox, which the finding graded backwards.

5. MATERIALITY TO ANY PUBLIC QUESTION: none, in the direction the finding pushes. On participation, neither version implicates him. On cooperation, the sworn record supports MORE voluntary cooperation than §3.7 states, not less. Adopting the finding would have the file assert, about a man charged with nothing, that he curated what investigators saw and did not hand over his phone — the opposite of what Davis swore. An audit that only ever moves one way is a bias signal, so I log the confirmation explicitly: §3.7's "handed over his phone contents" is CONFIRMED at Tier 1 on the very date the section assigns.

CONFIRMATIONS LOGGED IN THE OTHER DIRECTION (for the source): the quoted words ARE verbatim in the Cox file at line 11; the speaker IS Cox on content ("We got him," "my state," closing "I'll now turn the microphone over to the director of the FBI, Kash Patel," and Patel's reply "Thank you, Governor"); the date IS 2025-09-12 on content (Patel's "33 hours," suspect encountered "September 12th in the early morning hours"). The finder's source work was sound. The inference from it was not.

ITEM A — PRECISION, and a chain-of-custody upgrade from T3 to T1 (this is where the real value is). §3.7's sentence is uncited and compresses a three-stage acquisition into one verb, and one stage is not his act at all. Cite Davis, day3 01:02:53-01:03:14 and day4 02:37:34-02:38:36, 02:58:03-03:00:49. ITEM A-BIS — A POINT BOTH PRIOR LENSES MISSED, and it further undercuts the itemised list. The Discord thread did not reach investigators only through Mr. Twiggs. Davis, day4 02:52:39-02:52:48: Q "did law enforcement send a subpoena to Discord?" A "Yes, they did." Q "Were these messages recovered via that subpoena?" A "They were." So "Discord material" as an item he handed over is at best partial — he showed it and it was photographed, and it was independently obtained from the platform. Any rewrite of §3.7 must not present the Discord thread as sole-sourced to him.

ITEM B — RECORDING-LAYER COMPLETENESS, at the width the source carries and no wider. The profile nowhere records the statement that prompted investigators to ask for the Discord messages. Supported text: "The probable-cause affidavit (Tier 1, affiant Brian Davis, entered 2025-09-12 07:18) records — and Gov. Cox read the same passage aloud almost verbatim at the September 12, 2025 press conference (Tier 2 recitation of the same document, not an independent account) — that the roommate told investigators Robinson 'made a joke on discord,' after which investigators asked if he would show them those messages." Mandatory limits: this is the affiant's third-person paraphrase of one remark, by an affiant who was not present; on its face it characterises what ROBINSON posted; the record does not identify which message, and establishes nothing about Mr. Twiggs' state of mind. It must NOT be rendered as "his own characterisation of the Discord material as a joke," which imputes minimisation to a man accused of nothing. Note for calibration that the joke/meme framing the profile already carries sits where the record puts it — in Robinson's own text at line 104, "The f***in messages are mostly a big meme."

ITEM C — the finding's bonus claim is refuted and §3.6 stands unchanged. Cox's "Investigators identified... Investigators interviewed" establishes only that contact was investigator-initiated; it does not corroborate the relative's stronger claim that authorities "had to locate him and bring him in," and Davis's "he provided his phone... voluntarily" cuts the other way. Leave the "not officially confirmed" marking as is.

verdicts.reason:
REFUTED as framed. The finding's operative proposition is a CONTRADICTION between Cox's 2025-09-12 account and §3.7's "handed over his phone contents." That proposition is false on the primary record, and the "joke" limb cannot contradict a mechanism claim at all — it is an unrelated completeness observation bundled into a contradiction headline.

1. MECHANISM LIMB — false. I read the Cox transcript end to end. His narration (line 11) is one paragraph covering ONE step: investigators identified the roommate, interviewed him, he said Robinson "made a joke on Discord," investigators asked to see the Discord messages, he opened it, showed several, and allowed investigators to photograph the screen as each message was shown. I then went to the sworn record myself rather than take the earlier passes' quotations. Day 3 (Q&A structure; questioner asks, the case agent answers in first person about investigative steps — speaker inferred from content, label agrees): "Do you know if his phone was taken from him?" / "It was." / "When did that happen?" / "So It was during that interview with FBI at St. George Police Department. They conducted an interview of him and then he provided his phone. He did it voluntarily also, provided it to those agents." / "And that would've been on September 12th, 2025?" / "Correct." Day 4 completes the chain: at the first interview "he shows them the phone and then allows them to photograph the phone" (photos by an FBI agent, named in the transcript); and then "his phone is recovered at that point, taken into evidence… The FBI transported that phone to the RCFL… The phone was downloaded through Cellebrite… SBI received a flash drive containing that download. From there, it went to a SIAC analyst… And at that point that this image of this letter was located." Cox's passage and §3.7 describe SEQUENTIAL STEPS OF ONE INTERVIEW, not competing accounts.

2. COX'S SILENCE IS CHRONOLOGICAL, NOT CONTRADICTORY. Cox spoke the morning of 09-12; the affidavit carrying the identical passage was entered 09-12 07:18; the download happened "the following day or shortly after." Neither could describe a step that had not occurred. Per the project's absence rule, a press-conference summary of the identification chain is not a search space that would necessarily contain the phone handover, so its silence is not evidence of absence.

3. THE FINDING UNDER-GRADED ITS OWN SOURCE. The passage Cox read is verbatim in the affidavit of probable cause (T1 primary filing) — verified under BOTH the U+FFFE join and hyphen readings via artifact_search.find(). Treating it as a T2 press-conference statement in tension with the file is backwards; it is the same T1 text.

4. LIVING-PERSONS LENS — this is the decisive objection, and it runs in the direction the finding did not check. Adopting the finding would put MORE of a private individual's personal conduct into the file on a WEAKER basis, and would simultaneously make the file describe LESS cooperation than the sworn record supports. (a) The grammatical subject of "made a joke" is Robinson, not Twiggs — the affidavit is explicit, "his roommate (referring to Robinson) made a joke on discord." Rendering it as "the roommate's own 'joke' characterisation" converts a report about someone else's post into a stance by him about the evidence, which reads as minimisation and imports a state of knowledge the source does not carry. (b) The chain of transmission is at least three removes: him → the FBI agents in the room → the case agent, who testified under oath "No, I was not there" and worked from the recording and one agent's account → the affidavit → Cox reading it aloud. Nothing identifies WHICH message he was describing. (c) Reading "as each message was shown by Robinson's roommate" as gatekeeping imports reluctance the next step of the same interview defeats.

5. VERIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS; CONFIRMATIONS LOGGED. I searched for what would SUPPORT the finding as hard as against it. The only phrase capable of carrying its gatekeeping reading is the affidavit's "as each message was shown by Robinson's roommate" — defeated by the voluntary provision of the whole device minutes later and its full extraction. Confirmations found for the profile: §3.7's Sept. 12 date is independently confirmed at T1 ("The first time was the early morning hours of September 12th, and that occurred at St. George Police Department"); §3.7's "handed over his phone contents" is substantially T1-supported; §3.7's "Cox … publicly credited this material within days" is confirmed as to "publicly" and "within days" by this very transcript, though Cox never says "central" — that word remains the file's characterisation.

6. ABSENCE CLAIMS RE-RUN MYSELF (not inherited). Over the profile, capable patterns: "jok" → 1 hit only (his own quoted text at L91, so the pattern demonstrably matches the word "joke"); "joke" → 0; synonyms meme→1 (Robinson's own words, L100), prank/kidding→0. Also 0: Cellebrite, RCFL, SIAC, the interviewing agent's name, "St. George PD"/"St. George Police", "into evidence", "photo of the screen". So the joke remark, the screen-photography step and the custody chain are genuinely absent — but that is a completeness gap sourced to Days 3/4 and the affidavit, not a contradiction sourced to Cox. Over the two charging artifacts, both readings tested: the Information never mentions Discord (null under both) and says only that the roommate "received messages from Robinson about the shooting and provided those messages to police."

RESIDUAL SCOPE: I did not re-verify the profile's AP/NewsNation/ABC4 secondary citations, the April 20 2026 second-interview content, or whether any consent form or warrant governed retention of the device after the voluntary provision; the Day 3 testimony is the only sworn account of the taking that I read. I did not open day1/day2/day5, the contempt-hearing transcript, or the defence brief for this question. I excluded the mis-banked BAM Franchising artifact from all folder-level searches.
verdicts.corrected_form:
The finding must NOT be adopted: drop the contradiction claim entirely, and do not merge the surviving items back into it — they are sourced to the hearing transcripts and the affidavit, not to the Cox press conference, and they belong with the Q-144 banked items rather than to this finding.

What is adoptable instead, in the form that carries the least about him consistent with accuracy:

(1) COMPLETENESS, NOT CORRECTION — §3.7 compresses a documented three-step acquisition into one clause. "He handed over his phone contents: the text thread, the photo of the note, and Discord material" should become: "At the September 12, 2025 interview at St. George Police Department, Twiggs showed investigators the messages on his phone and allowed an FBI agent to photograph the screen as each message was displayed; he then voluntarily provided the phone itself. The phone was taken into evidence, transported by the FBI to the Regional Computer Forensic Laboratory and downloaded via Cellebrite, and a DPS SIAC analyst subsequently located the image of Robinson's note within that download." Tier 1 (sworn testimony, Days 3 and 4, read directly; speakers inferred from content). Confidence: High. The only substantive accuracy gain is that the note photo was NOT an item he selected and handed over — it was found by analyst search of the device he had provided; the itemised verb currently assigns him an affirmative act he did not perform. Note this change ADDS documented cooperation rather than subtracting it.

(2) THE "JOKE" REMARK — omittable, and omission is the least-carrying option. It answers no public question §3.7 raises: the public question is how the material reached investigators, and item (1) answers that completely. If the project nevertheless wants the provenance trigger on the record, it belongs in §3.4 (provenance of the Discord material) at the recording layer only, never in §3.7's cooperation narrative, and in this form: "The probable-cause affidavit records — and Gov. Cox read the same passage aloud on September 12, 2025 — that investigators asked the roommate to show them Discord messages after he told them Robinson had 'made a joke on discord.' The word describes Robinson's post, not the evidence as a whole; the affiant testified he was not present at the interview; the record does not identify which message was meant and establishes nothing about what Twiggs knew or believed." Confidence: High as to the fact that the statement was made; the referent is unestablished. It must never be rendered as his quoted words, as "his own characterisation," or as a stance toward the confession, the note or the texts.

(3) LEAVE §3.6 UNCHANGED. Cox's "investigators identified… investigators interviewed" establishes only that the contact was investigator-initiated. It does not corroborate the relative's stronger claim that authorities had to locate him and bring him in, which implies a reluctance the sworn record cuts against. The "not officially confirmed" marking stands.

(4) MINOR, ALSO VERIFIED: §3.7's "Cox and Bongino publicly credited this material within days as central to establishing the case" — "publicly" and "within days" are confirmed by the 2025-09-12 transcript; "as central" is the file's characterisation and Cox does not say it. Tighten or attribute.
